home.label: home
senses: Toast had been made and left to go cold on the side. The butter was still soft
The radiator ticked as it cooled, and a mug on the arm of the chair held a skin of tea
A pair of slippers waited at the foot of the stairs, toes pointed at the door, as if their owner meant to be back
The house smelled of floor polish, wet wool and a coal fire gone to ash
A kettle was still warm. A television somewhere murmured to nobody
Someone had started the washing and left it in the drum, damp, forgotten
A calendar by the fridge was marked in three colours of ink: dentist, bins, a birthday
The curtains were open on a garden full of dew, and the lamp was still on in daylight
plans: a calendar with a dentist's appointment circled for Thursday
a shopping list on the table, half crossed through
a casserole dish by the sink, soaking, for a Sunday that now would not come
a birthday card on the mantel, signed and not yet posted

waterfront.label: the water's edge
senses: Diesel, rope and weed; the water slapped the pilings in a slow, sleepy count
Gulls were quarrelling over something on the slip; a mooring line creaked like a door
A kettle sat on a camping stove, still warm, beside a thermos with a dented cup
The tide-table nailed to the shed wall had been ticked in pencil up to yesterday
Fog lay on the lake like a lid, and every sound inside it was close and flat
plans: a tide-chart with a boat booked out for Sunday
a ferry rota with their name pencilled in for next week
a coil of new rope, still tagged, and a receipt for it dated yesterday

shop.label: the shop
senses: The shop smelled of oil, brass and cardboard; the little bell above the door was still stilled
Shelves of small neat things, each in its place, and one gap among them like a missing tooth
A radio on the workbench was talking low about the weather over the lake
There was a sticker on the till: BACK IN FIVE. It had been there some time
The light through the window had a dusty gold in it and the whole place held still
plans: a delivery docket for Monday, signed in advance
an order book with next week's repairs pencilled in
a 'sale' sign half-lettered on the counter, the marker still beside it

tavern.label: the bar
senses: Stale beer, lemon and floor cleaner; the stools were still up on the tables, legs in the air
A glass stood on the bar with a quarter inch of whiskey in it and a ring still wet underneath
The jukebox hummed and clicked, hunting for a song nobody had asked for
Last night's ash was cold in the trays, and the blinds had been drawn against the morning
The cellar door was ajar and a cold draught came up it, smelling of mud
plans: a chalkboard with Friday's quiz night already lettered up
a keg order scribbled on a beer mat, with a smiley face
next week's rota on the wall, with their name in every other column

diner.label: the diner
senses: The griddle was still faintly warm; the room smelled of onions, coffee and old fat
Plates were stacked in the rack in the half-dark, still beaded with water
A pot of soup stood on the back ring with a skin on it, a ladle standing up in it like a flag
The coffee machine gave one long tired sigh and went quiet
Pies sat under glass domes. A single slice had been taken and not finished
plans: a menu for the week lettered on a board, with their name beside Saturday's special
the staff rota with their name written against every late shift
a delivery of flour and eggs stacked in the doorway, signed for

bakery.label: the bakery
senses: Yeast, scorched sugar and warm flour: the room had been baking since three, and nobody was there to take it out
Loaves stood on the racks gone dark and hard, and a timer was still counting backward
A fine white film lay on everything, and a single set of prints crossed it and stopped
The ovens ticked as they cooled. Somewhere in the walls a pipe ran like a stream
The window was fogged from inside, and in the fog someone had written nothing, carefully, with a finger
plans: an order slip for a wedding cake, due Saturday
a tray of buns marked for the school, wrapped and tied with string
a bake plan for the week in a neat hand, every day filled

studio.label: the studio
senses: Cold coffee, dust on the equalisers, the green glow of a dozen needles at rest
The soundproofing swallowed every footstep; the room sounded like the inside of a held breath
A pair of headphones hung round the neck of the chair, still faintly hissing
The red light over the door was on, and nobody could say why
A reel of tape had run off its spool and lay across the floor in long brown curls
plans: tomorrow's running order, typed, with their slot circled
a pile of ads to be voiced, each tagged with a sticky note
a birthday dedication on the request list, to be read on air at noon

dam.label: the dam
senses: Damp concrete, machine oil and a cold that came up through the soles; the turbines hummed on a single low note
Water ran somewhere in the walls, and the gauges ticked, patient and exact
A flask and a paperback lay on the console. The page was marked at a chapter about drowning
The inspection lamp on its hook swung gently though there was no wind in the gallery
The air smelled of rust and lake, and your voice came back a moment after you spoke
plans: an inspection sheet for next week, already half filled out
a maintenance schedule with their name against every Thursday
a leave request for the lake festival, signed and approved

civic.label: the office
senses: Paper, toner and radiator heat; a clock ticked on the wall with a slightly embarrassed air
Index cards stood in long drawers like organ pipes, and a stamp-pad lay open and drying
A stack of forms waited under a paperweight; the top one was half filled in
The room had the hush of a place that is always about to be asked a question
Dust moved slowly in the light from the single high window
plans: a diary with a leave request filed for the lake festival
a Monday schedule on the desk, every hour accounted for
a half-written memo with a deadline of Friday

theatre.label: the playhouse
senses: Dust, glue and old velvet, with the ghost light burning on the stage like a single patient eye
Costumes hung in rows, still faintly breathing out their last wearers' scent
The ropes of the fly-loft creaked as something very high up settled itself
A kettle in the wings, a cigarette stub in a saucer, a script open face down
The house seats were all tipped up, and in the dark they looked like rows of folded hands
plans: a rehearsal call-sheet for Tuesday with their name highlighted
the poster for opening night, signed by the whole cast
a costume fitting booked, written in lipstick on the dressing-room mirror

medical.label: the clinic
senses: Antiseptic, boiled linen and the faint sweetness of something under it; a machine somewhere gave a patient, regular beep
The blinds were down and the strip light buzzed a quarter-tone flat
A tray of instruments was laid out under a cloth, neat, as if for a procedure that had been put off
A cup of tea had gone cold on the nurses' desk beside a page of handover notes
The floor had been mopped and still smelled of pine; the mop bucket stood by the door, the water grey
plans: an appointment book with next week filled in, name by name
a rota with their name against the whole of the weekend
a hand-written card, 'get well soon', waiting to be sent to someone else

funeral.label: the funeral home
senses: Lilies, polish and a cold that had nothing to do with the weather; the carpet swallowed every footstep
A bell chimed softly somewhere in the building, for no reason anyone could find
The long room was silent, and the silence had a courteous, waiting quality
A guest book lay open on its stand, and beside it a pen on a chain
Curtains of heavy velvet hung motionless, and the air smelled of cut stems
plans: a service sheet for Thursday, drafted and left on the blotter
a diary with three arrangements pencilled in, one of them still blank
an order for white roses, to be delivered on the weekend

school.label: the school
senses: Chalk, floor wax and a small, sour trace of milk; tiny coats hung from tiny pegs in the dim
The radiators clanked and the heating pipes knocked in long, slow sentences
The clock over the board ticked loud enough to be a person in the room
A child's painting of a house by a lake was taped to the glass, the colours still wet
A bell, unrung, hung over the door, and the whole building seemed to be listening for it
plans: a lesson plan for Monday, written in a careful hand
a stack of marked exercise books with a sticker chart on top
a parents' evening schedule with their slot circled

chapel.label: the chapel
senses: Beeswax and cold stone; the light through the lake window lay across the pews like a spilled drink
The organ breathed once, a long soft breath from a pipe nobody was touching
A single candle guttered in a draught that had no business in a shut church
Hymn numbers stood on the board for a service that would not now be taken
The air was heavy with the smell of old hymnals and, beneath it, the lake
plans: a sermon draft for Sunday, the last paragraph unwritten
a service rota with their name against every week of the month
a funeral booking for Friday in a hand not their own

sheriff.label: the Sheriff's office
senses: Burnt coffee, gun oil and carbon paper; the radio on the shelf crackled and rested like a sleeping animal
A cell door stood ajar and the thin grey light of morning lay on the bunk like a sheet
The fluorescent tube flickered over the dispatch desk, and the log still lay open to last night
A phone rang once on a desk with nobody at it, and stopped
The wall clock was exactly right, which in this town was the strangest thing in the room
plans: a duty roster with their name in every night shift for the month
a stack of reports to be filed on Monday, in three colours of ink
a retirement card signed by half the town, waiting on the desk

hall.label: the Grange hall
senses: Floor polish and stacked chairs; a long trestle table stood ready for a supper nobody had come to eat
The tea urn gurgled and clicked into silence, and the bunting stirred overhead though the doors were shut
The raffle tickets were still in their drum, and the drum was still turning
A folding screen leaned against the wall and behind it something had been put away carefully
The place smelled of damp wool, jam, and a century of other people's gatherings
plans: a notice for the harvest supper, in their handwriting, pinned to the board
a booking sheet for the hall with their name in the next three Saturdays
a float of coins in a biscuit tin for the raffle, counted and labelled

generic.label: the place
senses: The room held the faint sourness of a place left suddenly
Light came grey through a dusty window and the clock ticked as if nothing had happened
plans: a diary with next week filled in
a pencilled note on the desk about Friday
